confidence.rationale: Both restaurant-issued PDFs were reopened. The frozen baseline is sourced from a chart revised May 13, 2016, while the current 2025 U.S. guide provides a materially different allergen matrix. This confirms a baseline discrepancy, although Terra's classification of every item as a location mismatch is unsupported.

confirmedFindings: Affected baseline items (37): Almond; Blue Raspberry Beverages; Breakfast Sandwich; Caramel; Cheddar Cheese Stuffed Nuggets; Cheese Sauce; Cinnamon Sugar; Clarified Butter; Coke Products; Frozen Lemonade; Frozen Mocha; Heated Cheese Sauce; Hot Salsa Cheese Sauce; Iced Tea Bag-in-Box; Iced Tea Brewed; Jalapeño; Latte Products; Lemonade Mixers; Light Cream Cheese; Mango Beverages; Marinara Sauce; Non-Stick Spray; Original; Pepperoni; Piña Colada Beverages; Pretzel Dog; Pretzels Without Butter; Pretzels With Butter; Raisin; Roasted Garlic Parmesan; Shake Products; Sour Cream and Onion; Stabilizer; Strawberry Beverages; Sweet Mustard; Sweet Pretzel Dip; Wild Cherry Beverages.
The frozen baseline's sole allergen source is marked “Confidential Revised 05.13.16,” while the restaurant-issued current guide is dated March 2025 and contains a newer allergen matrix.
The current guide differs materially from the frozen source in product structure and allergen coverage, so the frozen allergen claims cannot be treated as verified current U.S. national data.
A discrepancy therefore exists and the packet's effectiveOutcome is upheld.
rejectedFindings: Terra's assertion that all 37 items are location mismatches is not supported. The older document is hosted on the Mexico domain, but its content identifies Auntie Anne's LLC, supplies a U.S. customer-service number, and does not identify a Mexico-specific menu.

Several baseline concepts remain explicitly present in the current U.S. guide, including Original, Cinnamon Sugar, Sweet Almond, Jalapeño, Pepperoni, Pretzel Dog, breakfast sandwiches, Caramel, Cheese, Hot Salsa Cheese, Marinara, Cream Cheese, Frozen Lemonade, and lemonade mixers. These cannot all be reconciled as location mismatches.
The evidence establishes staleness and item-level changes, not that every baseline item belongs to the wrong geographic scope.

additionalEvidence.summary: Current restaurant-issued guide dated March 2025. It identifies auntieannes.com and Auntie Anne's Franchisor SPV LLC, and provides current nutrition and allergen matrices on pages 7–8.

Frozen baseline source containing the 37 labels. Its footer says “Auntie Anne's LLC — Confidential Revised 05.13.16.” It does not label itself as a Mexico-specific menu and lists the U.S. customer-service number.
Official U.S. menu page reopened, but it exposed no stable menu text suitable for independent row-level reconciliation.

summary: The discrepancy_found outcome is confirmed because the 37-item baseline relies on a 2016 allergen chart that is not adequate evidence for current U.S. claims. Terra's blanket location-mismatch rationale is rejected: the source's hosting domain alone does not establish Mexican scope, and numerous baseline products remain in the current U.S. guide.
